title: Molecular weight determination of lignin via gel permeation chromatography
author: Lisa M. Stanley
materials: Standards Prepare polystyrene (PS) stock solutions by grouping the eighteen PS standards with varying molecular weights as shown in Table 1. Dissolve 5 mg of each standard in the group into 50 mL of tetrahydrofuran (THF) along with 1 mL of toluene. Transfer 1 mL of each stock solution to a 2 mL amber GC vial. These will be used to create the calibration curve. Stock solutions should be kept in a refrigerator capable of maintaining a temperature of 4 °C.

steps.title: Acetylate Lignocellulosic Material
steps.instruction: Perform acetylation on air-dried lignocellulosic material to prepare it for GPC analysis.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 20 mg of air-dried lignocellulosic material in a mixture of 0.5 mL pyridine and 0.5 mL acetic anhydride in 5 mL conical vials.
Heat vials at 40 °C in a heating and stirring module for 24 h with stirring.
Terminate the reaction by adding 0.2 mL of methanol.
Add 1 mL aliquots of methanol to each sample and dry under nitrogen; repeat methanol additions 7-10 times.
Dry samples in a vacuum oven at 40 °C overnight.

steps.title: Prepare Samples for GPC
steps.instruction: Suspend acetylated samples in THF and filter for injection.

substeps.instruction: Suspend dried, acetylated samples in THF to a final dilution of 2 mg of lignin residue per 1 mL of THF.
Filter samples through a 0.2 µm PTFE filter into a GC vial.
If insoluble material remains, collect the solids before filtering the liquids through a 0.2 μm filter.
Dry and weigh the collected solids to determine the ratio of sample not represented in the GPC analysis.

steps.title: Purge HPLC System
steps.instruction: Eliminate air from the Agilent 1260 series HPLC system by purging solvent lines.

substeps.instruction: Bypass the columns and increase the THF flow rate from 1.0 mL/min to 2.5 mL/min in 0.5 mL increments.
Reduce the flow rate to 0.2 mL/min.
Return the columns to the flow path.
Increase the flow rate by 0.2 mL/min increments until a final flow rate of 1.0 mL/min is reached.

steps.title: Configure GPC Run and Autosampler
steps.instruction: Set up the autosampler vials and define the injection sequence for standards and samples.

substeps.instruction: Fill the first autosampler vial with THF (for needle cleaning) and the second with THF (for 3-5 initial blanks).
Place five PS standard solutions (PS1 to PS5) after the THF vials.
Sequence the run: start with two runs of PS1, then run PS1 through PS5 in order.
Place samples after the standards.
Run a PS5 standard after every ten samples and again at the end of the run to monitor instrument drift.
Finish with one THF blank to clear residues, then shut down the system.

steps.title: Perform GPC Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze lignin components using the specified HPLC parameters.

substeps.instruction: Set the total run time for each sample to 40 minutes.
Set the detection wavelength to 260 nm with a bandwidth of 80 nm.
If the peak retention times of the five PS5 standards at the end of the run are +/-0.1 minute out of range of each other, re-run the samples that occurred after the deviation.

steps.title: Process GPC Data
steps.instruction: Analyze the resulting data using specialized software.

substeps.instruction: Use Agilent Cirrus GPC Offline GPC/SEC software version 3.4.1 and Agilent OpenLab CDS, ChemStation Edition version 1.167.13.0 (or alternative GPC software).
